free_tier.stated: NAT IPv4 128 MB, the entry row of the vendor's own NAT table: 128 MB RAM, 1 vCore, a shared IPv4 with 20 forwarded ports plus SSH, a /80 IPv6, 2 GB of storage, 125 GB of bandwidth, at USD 3.50 to 5.00 a year depending on location. Locations: Bulgaria, Canada, Chicago, Germany, Finland, France, New York, Netherlands, Poland, Singapore. The 256 MB row is USD 6.50 to 10 a year with 4 GB and 250 GB, the 512 MB row USD 12.50 to 20 with 8 GB and 500 GB, and the 1024 MB row USD 24.50 to 40 with 12 GB and 1000 GB. The KVM NAT table starts higher, at 384 MB for USD 15 a year. The tracker lists the 128 MB plan at USD 0.29 a month on a yearly term with 2 GB HDD and a 0.1 Gbps port in the U.S.A., Canada and Germany.

egress.terms: 125 GB of bandwidth stated on the row with no period in the table header; the tracker reads it as monthly. No overage rate is published

tooling: NAT VPS: no public IPv4 of its own, 20 forwarded ports plus SSH, /80 IPv6. Enough for an outbound-only worker or a reverse tunnel, not for anything that needs to accept traffic on arbitrary ports
chaining: at USD 3.50 a year this is the cheapest way to get a machine with outbound network access in ten countries it is a tunnel endpoint, a monitor or a cron runner, not a crawler, because 125 GB and a NAT port list cap it

limits.value: 125 GB of bandwidth is the wall, and it arrives before any CPU or disk limit matters; the shared IPv4 exposes only 20 forwarded ports plus SSH, so the host cannot be reached on arbitrary ports at all
